A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-G. The material supports a reliable comparison throughout.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original explanation-generation experiments, reward-model sensitivity analyses, prompting ablations, and failure-case investigations in Sections 3-4 and Appendices D-G.

after.justification: v2.pdf retains these original empirical results, including quantitative comparisons in Tables 1-7 and qualitative reward-model investigations in Figures 3-6.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same two-step attribute-conditioned perturbation method, preference-flip categorization into counterfactuals and semifactuals, and procedures for global sensitivity and representative-example selection. The operational prompts in Appendix B are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate on HelpSteer2, HH-RLHF-helpful, and HH-RLHF-harmless. The single-turn task coverage and the harmful-content, privacy, and disrespectful-language investigation scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 1-2 retain the same Polyjuice and random GPT-4o perturbation comparisons, including the absence of Polyjuice rows for HelpSteer2. Appendix G retains the same reward-model comparisons, including LlamaOB and LlamaSW.

E3.justification: Sampling, filtering, model sizes, 15 perturbations per response, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Both retain sampling 500 comparisons per dataset before agreement filtering for global analysis and the 110-comparison disrespectful-language test.

E4.justification: Appendices D-G retain the same prompting ablation, correct-versus-wrong preference analysis, chosen-versus-rejected sensitivity comparison, and larger-model failure investigations. The representative case studies in Section 4 are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report five repetitions with different random seeds and summarize the quantitative evaluation using means and standard deviations. No run-count disclosure, uncertainty-reporting practice, or statistical test is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1-7 and result Figures 3-6 retain their numerical entries and findings. For example, Table 1 preserves OURS's both-response CF coverage of 0.69, 0.80, and 0.33 on harmless, helpful, and HelpSteer2, respectively.

T1.justification: Section 1 removes 'minimally' from its counterfactual definition and 'maximally' from its semifactual definition, relaxing those introductory conditions. This is a limited definitional correction; Section 2.2's formal set definitions and the subsequent mathematical calculations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about explaining reward-model comparisons, generating attribute-conditioned perturbations, and obtaining local and global insights. No main contribution or claimed empirical advantage is added or withdrawn.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretations of the locality-diversity tradeoff, dataset-dependent sensitivities, and model failures. The limitations concerning lack of guaranteed counterfactuals and coarse semifactual categorization in Section 5 are unchanged.

D1.justification: The attribute-selection procedure, full prompts, experimental details, and model-access links are unchanged. Section 2.3's more explicit pointer to Appendix A's descriptions and justifications references information already present in v1.pdf.

R1.justification: No cited works are added or removed, and the positioning relative to text counterfactuals, reward decomposition, global recourse, and feature importance is retained. The citation-format and connective-wording edits do not alter these relationships.

P1.justification: Small edits revise the introductory definitions, contribution lead-in, appendix references, and paragraph-heading punctuation. The running header changes from 'Preprint' to the ICLR 2025 publication statement, and affiliation markers change. Section order and nearly all prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 3 has wider column spacing, while Figure 1 and several tables shift slightly with text reflow. All six figures and seven tables remain, with unchanged graphical content and only limited layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: Removing the introductory minimality/maximality conditions makes the CF/SF descriptions consistent with Section 2.2's existing preference-flip definitions, reducing a small conceptual inconsistency. Clearer appendix pointers also aid navigation. The empirical evidence, procedures, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
